questions.text: Which device is used to type letters into a computer?
questions.explanation: A keyboard is the input device for typing.

questions.text: Which of these is an output device?
questions.explanation: A printer produces output on paper.

questions.text: What does CPU stand for?
questions.explanation: CPU means Central Processing Unit.

questions.text: Which of these is an example of an operating system?
questions.explanation: Windows manages the computer hardware and software.

questions.text: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
questions.explanation: The heart pumps blood.

questions.text: What do plants need to make their food?
questions.explanation: Plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide.

questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for water?
questions.explanation: Water is two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.text: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.

questions.text: Choose the correct plural of 'child'.
questions.explanation: 'Children' is the irregular plural of child.

questions.text: Which word is a noun?
questions.explanation: A noun names a thing; table is a thing.

questions.text: Which word is closest in meaning to 'happy'?
questions.explanation: Joyful is a synonym of happy.

questions.text: Identify the verb: 'The dog runs fast.'
questions.explanation: Runs is the action word.

questions.text: Simplify: 2/3 + 1/6
Solve for x: 2x − 7 = 11
What is the area of a rectangle 8 cm long and 5 cm wide?
questions.explanation: Area = length × width = 8 × 5 = 40 cm².

questions.text: Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to 'generous'.
questions.explanation: Selfish is the opposite of generous.

questions.text: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: After 'doesn't' the verb stays in its base form.

questions.text: What is the plural of 'tooth'?
questions.explanation: 'Teeth' is the irregular plural of tooth.

questions.text: Which part of a plant absorbs water from the soil?
questions.explanation: Roots take in water and minerals from the soil.

questions.text: What is the process by which liquid water changes to water vapour?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is a liquid changing into a gas.

questions.text: Which of these is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Metals such as copper conduct electricity well.

questions.text: If log₁₀ 1000 = x, find x.
Find the gradient of the line y = 3x + 5.
questions.explanation: In y = mx + c the gradient is m, which is 3.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ present.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the nearer subject, "students", so "were" is used.

questions.text: Which word is closest in meaning to 'diligent'?
questions.explanation: A diligent person works carefully and hard.

questions.text: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Mass has size only; velocity, force and displacement also have direction.

questions.text: What is the chemical formula of sodium chloride?
questions.explanation: One sodium ion combines with one chloride ion: NaCl.

questions.text: A teacher checks learners’ understanding during a lesson so that she can adjust her teaching. This is called:
questions.explanation: Formative assessment happens during learning and guides what the teacher does next.

questions.text: Which of these is a clear learning objective?
options: By the end of the lesson, pupils will add two fractions with the same denominator.
questions.explanation: A good objective states what learners will be able to do, and can be checked.

questions.text: Which action best supports an inclusive classroom?
options: Seat struggling learners at the back
Use varied activities so all learners can take part
Teach only to the fastest learners
Excuse some learners from taking part
questions.explanation: Varied activities give every learner a way to take part and learn.

questions.text: Keeping accurate records of learners’ attendance and progress mainly helps a teacher to:
options: Track progress and support learners who fall behind
questions.explanation: Good records show who needs extra help and whether teaching is working.

questions.text: A lesson plan should be prepared:
options: Only at the end of term
questions.explanation: Planning ahead keeps the lesson focused on its objectives.

questions.text: In school supervision, clinical supervision primarily focuses on:
options: Collaborative improvement of classroom instruction between supervisor and teacher
questions.explanation: Clinical supervision is a developmental, collaborative process aimed at improving teaching practice.

questions.text: Which body in Ghana is responsible for formulating and implementing pre-tertiary education policies under the Ministry of Education?
questions.explanation: The Ghana Education Service (GES) implements approved national pre-tertiary educational policies and programmes.

questions.text: Strategic educational planning at the directorate level begins with:
options: Disbursing capitation grants without a budget
Conducting a comprehensive situational analysis and needs assessment
questions.explanation: A situational analysis and needs assessment establish baseline data and priorities before setting strategic goals.

questions.text: The aim of Ghana's system of education is …………..
questions.explanation: Ghana's education system is designed to develop personality, build character, and preserve culture, so all three combine into the correct answer.

questions.text: The ministry of Education of Ghana, which is a multi-portfolio government ministry, was established in ……..
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Education, as a multi-portfolio ministry, was established in 1957, around Ghana's independence period.

questions.text: Which of the following is/are the objective(s) of the 1987 Education Reform? I. Increase access to basic education II. Shorten the pre-tertiary education structure from 17 years to 12 years III. Make education cost-effective IV. Improve the quality of education by making it more relevant to socio-economic conditions
questions.explanation: The 1987 Education Reform pursued all four objectives listed, aiming to expand access, shorten the structure, cut costs and improve quality.

questions.text: How many functional divisions does the Ghana Education Service have at the headquarters?
questions.explanation: The Ghana Education Service Headquarters is organised into 7 functional divisions.

questions.text: The performance of a student can be evaluated in the best possible manner through………
questions.explanation: Continuous Assessment, carried out throughout a term, gives the most complete picture of a student's performance over time.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a body under the Ministry of Education which implements its policies and programmes?
questions.explanation: The Teacher Education Division (TED) is not one of the bodies directly under the Ministry of Education implementing its programmes; it is domiciled at GES/GTEC.

questions.text: Testing in education is only possible by using ………
questions.explanation: A Standardized Achievement Test provides uniform, validated conditions for testing, which is why it is singled out as the correct option.

questions.text: How many units has the Technical and Vocational Education Division (TVED) of the Ghana Education Service (GES) Headquarters?
questions.explanation: The Technical and Vocational Education Division (TVED) at GES Headquarters comprises 7 units.

questions.text: Which of the following is/are not the objective(s) of the Free Compulsory Universal Basic Education (FCUBE)? I. Improving the quality of learning and teaching II. Improving access to basic education facilities III. Encouraging private sector participation in the provision of education facilities IV. Improving management efficiency
questions.explanation: FCUBE aimed to improve quality, access and management efficiency; encouraging private sector participation was not one of its stated objectives.

questions.text: Which one of the following Acts established the Ghana Education Service in 1995?
questions.explanation: The Ghana Education Service was established under GES Act 506 of 1995.

questions.text: Which of the following is/are not the way(s) through which education policies are formulated? I. Imposition by elites II. Political discussions III. Stakeholder consultations
questions.explanation: Sound education policy formulation relies on political discussion and stakeholder consultation; imposition by elites is not a legitimate way policies are formulated.

questions.text: How many divisions are under the jurisdiction of the Deputy Director-General (Quality and Access) of the Ghana Education Service?
questions.explanation: Four divisions fall under the Deputy Director-General (Quality and Access) at GES Headquarters.

questions.text: Curriculum provides guidance for …………..
questions.explanation: Curriculum chiefly guides teachers in what and how to teach within a given period.

questions.text: Psychological foundation plays its role in the development of curriculum, keeping in view of the …….
questions.explanation: The psychological foundation of curriculum design takes into account learners' needs, interests and capabilities all together.

questions.text: An outline of the topics of a subject to be covered in a specific time is called a ……….
questions.explanation: An outline of topics to be covered within a specific time frame is properly called a curriculum in this context.

questions.text: All of the following statements regarding a teacher are correct except that the teacher
options: Changes his/her attitudes and behaviour according to the needs of the society
Is a friend, guide and philosopher
Is the leader of the class
questions.explanation: A good teacher builds on and extends what students already know rather than simply teaching only what they already know.

questions.text: The type of education acquired without any specific purpose, fixed period is called
questions.explanation: Informal education is acquired without any specific purpose or fixed period, unlike formal schooling.

questions.text: Why are co-curricular activities used in teaching?
options: To make teaching interesting and effective
questions.explanation: Co-curricular activities are used mainly to make teaching more interesting and effective for learners.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences is/are correct about the nature of teaching? I. It is remedial II. It is diagnostic III. It is both remedial and diagnostic
questions.explanation: Teaching is both remedial (correcting gaps) and diagnostic (identifying problems), so all statements are correct.

questions.text: The procedure used to determine learner's abilities is referred to as
questions.explanation: A criterion-referenced test measures a learner's ability against a fixed standard, which is how learner abilities are determined here.

questions.text: What are the three components of educational process?
questions.explanation: The educational process is built on teaching, learning and practice working together.

questions.text: Teaching through the deductive method is done from the…..
questions.explanation: The deductive method moves from general principles to specific applications.

questions.text: A/an ……………. assessment is one which measures what is intended to measure.
questions.explanation: Validity refers to an assessment measuring exactly what it is intended to measure.

questions.text: The use of technology to enhance the learning process is called ……… in education.
questions.explanation: Using technology to enhance learning is known as Information Communication Technology (ICT) in education.

questions.text: The purpose of evaluation in education is to ……..
options: Assign a mark or score to a student
Make judgement about the quality of learning
Test the students in a subject
questions.explanation: Evaluation in education is fundamentally about making a judgement on the quality of learning, beyond simply scoring or testing.

questions.text: According to John Dewey, the teacher should guide students in acquiring knowledge as a ………… in the learning process.
questions.explanation: John Dewey viewed the teacher's role as a facilitator who guides rather than dictates the learning process.

questions.text: The primary aim of educational psychology is to………….
options: Contribute to an understanding of sound educational practices
Provide the academic background essential for effective teaching
Provide a theoretical framework for educational research
Provide the teacher with a greater appreciation of his role in the education of the child
questions.explanation: Educational psychology primarily helps teachers appreciate their role in a child's education more deeply.

questions.text: The word "pedagogy" means to………..
questions.explanation: The word 'pedagogy' derives from the Greek for 'to lead the child'.

questions.text: A scoring guide to evaluate the quality of students is called ………
questions.explanation: A rubric is the scoring guide used to evaluate the quality of student work against set criteria.

questions.text: Teachers should present information to the students clearly and in interesting ways and relate new information to the things students………….
questions.explanation: Effective teaching connects new information to what students already know to aid understanding.

questions.text: The field of study which is concerned with the construction of thought processes, including remembering, problem solving and decision-making is called ………
questions.explanation: Cognitive development is the field concerned with thought processes such as remembering, problem-solving and decision-making.

questions.text: The process of obtaining numerical value for a characteristic is known as
questions.explanation: Measurement is the process of assigning a numerical value to a characteristic being assessed.

questions.text: In teaching, the discussion method can be used when ……….
questions.explanation: Discussion method works best when the topic is straightforward enough for learners to engage with productively.

questions.text: Which of the following is/are the main aim(s) of teaching?
questions.explanation: Teaching aims mainly to develop thinking and reasoning skills in learners, not merely transmit information.

questions.text: The quality of teaching is reflected by the
options: Attendance of students in the class
Duration of silence maintained in the class
Quality of questions asked by students
questions.explanation: The percentage of students who pass is a direct outcome measure reflecting the quality of teaching.

questions.text: A formal and systematic procedure of getting information is called………
questions.explanation: Testing is defined as a formal, systematic procedure for gathering information about learner performance.

questions.text: Which of the following is not considered a key behaviour essential for effective teaching?
options: Effective use of bulletin board space
questions.explanation: Bulletin board use is largely cosmetic and is not considered a core behaviour underpinning effective teaching, unlike clarity or instructional variety.

questions.text: An effective teacher is expected to ……..
options: Make students feel that education is their need
Reduce the anxiety level of students to a moderate level
questions.explanation: An effective teacher combines encouraging initiative, showing relevance, and managing anxiety — all of the above.

questions.text: An evaluation that monitors learning progress is referred to as ………….
questions.explanation: Formative evaluation is ongoing assessment used to monitor and guide learning progress.

questions.text: The main purpose of supervising teaching is to ……….
questions.explanation: Supervision of teaching is mainly meant to ensure the curriculum is properly carried out in classrooms.

questions.text: Mrs. Yamoah teaches Junior High School 3. When her students enter her classroom each day, they walk to their assigned desks and take their seats. Immediately, they take out their notebooks to write down and answer the questions on the board that reviews the previous day's lesson. While the students are quietly working, Mrs. Yamoah takes attendance. Once everyone has answered the question, Mrs. Yamoah reviews it with her class before moving on to the day's lesson. Which of the following terms accurately describes the situation above?
questions.explanation: Mrs Yamoah's consistent routines, clear expectations and structured start to lessons describe a well-managed classroom.

questions.text: Which of the following is not one of the core domains of the National Teachers' Standards?
questions.explanation: The National Teachers' Standards core domains are Professional Knowledge, Practice, and Values and Attitudes — Professional Ethics is not one of the named domains.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a tool for formative assessment in scholastic domain?
questions.explanation: Conversational skill is not a standard formative assessment tool compared with oral questions, projects, or MCQs.

questions.text: What was Ghana's score on the Corruption Perception Index (CPI) released by Transparency International in 2018?
questions.explanation: Ghana scored 41% on the 2018 Corruption Perceptions Index released by Transparency International.

questions.text: Which one of the following political ideologies is Plato credited with?
questions.explanation: Plato is historically credited with early ideas underpinning democracy through his political philosophy.

questions.text: The first important step in teaching is
options: Knowing the background of the students
questions.explanation: Effective teaching begins with knowing the background of the students before planning or delivering lessons.

questions.text: A newly posted teacher who is maltreated in his/her class by students should deal with them by ………..
options: Changing his/her class after consultation with the headteacher
Giving them a threat of expulsion
Improving his/her qualities and expressing them in a good way
questions.explanation: A maltreated teacher should respond by improving their own qualities and expressing them positively, rather than resorting to punitive measures.

questions.text: The main purpose of classroom assessment is to ………….
questions.explanation: Classroom assessment mainly exists to measure and improve teacher effectiveness and instructional practice.

questions.text: Where is the International Court of Justice situated?
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice is situated in The Hague, Netherlands.

questions.text: The term used for monitoring outcomes with reference to objectives is ………..
questions.explanation: Evaluation is the term used to describe monitoring outcomes against stated objectives.

questions.text: The Common Core Programme (CCP) for Junior and Senior High Schools consists of how many subjects?
questions.explanation: The Common Core Programme (CCP) for JHS and SHS is built around 9 core subjects.

questions.text: Which one of these agencies is not a body under the Ministry of Education which implements its policies and programmes related to education?
questions.explanation: The National Commission for Civic Education is not implementing agency under the Ministry of Education's education programmes.

questions.text: Which of the following is/are the objectives of the 1987 Education Reform? I. Increase access to basic education II. Shorten the pre-university education structure from 17 years to 12 years III. Make education cost effective IV. Improve quality of education by making it more relevant to socio-economic conditions.
questions.explanation: The 1987 Education Reform pursued all four listed objectives: access, structure, cost, and quality.

questions.text: Which of the following was part of the programmes and interventions implemented to facilitate the attainment of the Free Compulsory Universal Basic Education (FCUBE) policy objectives? I. Quality Improvement in Primary Schools (QUIPS) II. Child School Community Progress in Education (Child Scope) III. Performance Monitoring Test (PMT) IV. District Teacher Support Team (DTST)
questions.explanation: FCUBE's implementation involved QUIPS, Child Scope, PMT and DTST as supporting programmes and interventions.

questions.text: Ghana's system of education is aimed at which of these aspects of development?
questions.explanation: Ghana's education system targets character formation, personality development and preservation of culture together.

questions.text: Which of the following is/are not the way through which education policies are formulated? I. Imposition by elites II. Political discussions III. Stakeholder consultations
questions.explanation: Legitimate education policy formulation happens through political discussion and stakeholder consultation, not elite imposition.

questions.text: Which of the following subjects is not part of the list of subjects to be studied under the Common Core Programme for Junior and Senior High Schools in Ghana?
questions.explanation: History is not one of the subjects listed under the Common Core Programme for JHS/SHS.

questions.text: The current Deputy Director-General of the Ghana Education Service in charge of Quality and Access is known as
questions.explanation: Dr Kwabena Bempah Tandoh is the Deputy Director-General for Quality and Access at GES.

questions.text: Membership of the Ghana Education Service is made up of all the following except
options: Other persons that may be employed for the service
Teachers and non-teaching supporting personnel in pre-tertiary educational institutions in the public system
The personnel of the Ghana Education Service existing immediately before the coming into force of the Ghana Education Act of 1995
questions.explanation: Membership of GES excludes 'all stakeholders in education' as a category, since membership is specifically defined by statute.

questions.text: Which of the following is the least effective remedy for students' absenteeism in schools?
options: Parents should be counseled to ensure regular attendance of their wards/pupils to school
Parents should personally supervise the activities of their wards to ensure that they do not play truant
Pupils should be punished for absenteeism
Teachers should desist from harassing students
questions.explanation: Punishing pupils for absenteeism is a poor remedy compared with counselling and supervision, which address root causes.

questions.text: The headteacher in a learner-centered school undertakes all the following activities to enhance teaching and learning except
options: Empowering learners in the teaching/learning process
Encouraging teachers to avoid tests and other assessment because they demoralize students
Encouraging teachers to develop lesson plans that use existing knowledge to construct new knowledge
Motivating and sustaining teachers' interest in teaching
questions.explanation: A learner-centred headteacher would not encourage avoiding tests, since assessment supports learning rather than only demoralising students.

questions.text: Which one of the following is the most common role of teachers in education?
options: Build a warm environment in the classroom
Set the tone of their classrooms
questions.explanation: Mentoring and nurturing students is widely regarded as the most common role of a teacher.

questions.text: Which of the following is not one of the core competencies emphasized in the new standards-based curriculum?
questions.explanation: Clarity is a teaching quality rather than a core competency emphasised specifically in the new standards-based curriculum.

questions.text: Which of the following methods, techniques and principles are teachers encouraged to use to promote effective teaching and learning? I. Building on past learning or previous knowledge and positive reinforcement II. Providing guidance and practice in class before independent practice III. Motivating and sustaining pupils' interest IV. Involving each learner in the teaching and learning process V. Even distribution of evaluative questions
options: I, II, III, IV and V
I, II, III and IV only
questions.explanation: Effective teaching draws on all five listed methods, techniques and principles together.

questions.text: Supervision of teaching mainly ensures
questions.explanation: Supervision of teaching is mainly concerned with ensuring quality delivery of the curriculum.

questions.text: Management is commonly defined as
options: Getting things done so that demand is fulfilled
Getting things done through other people
Knowing what actually has been produced and what should have been produced
questions.explanation: Management is commonly defined as getting things done through other people.

questions.text: Rote learning is more common with …………….. curriculum.
questions.explanation: Rote learning is most common in subject-centred curricula that emphasise content coverage over understanding.

questions.text: All the following statements about the teacher are correct, except that the teacher
options: Is seen as a role model to pupils
Is the leader of the class
Serves as a facilitator to pupils' learning
questions.explanation: A good teacher facilitates learning rather than imposing ideas on pupils.

questions.text: Teaching objectives should be all the following, except being
questions.explanation: Teaching objectives should be achievable, realistic and time-bound, not rigid.

questions.text: The maturity of students determines the
options: Appropriate motivational techniques needed to be employed
questions.explanation: Student maturity influences motivational techniques, learning tasks and teaching methods all at once.

questions.text: Which one of the following reasons best explains why teachers should ensure that there are physical pathways for students in the classroom? The pathways
options: Allow students private space to work for themselves
Make it easier for teachers to attend to individual students' needs
Make it easier for teachers to see the board from the back
Make students less likely to become distracted
questions.explanation: Physical pathways in class make it easier for teachers to reach and support individual students.

questions.text: If teachers want to present information to students in interesting ways, they should start from what they
questions.explanation: Presenting information effectively starts from what students already know before building new content.

questions.text: In order to effect a purposeful change in schools, a school leader should ask the question
options: What do we hope to accomplish?
Why is the change taking place?
questions.explanation: Purposeful change begins with identifying what the school leader hopes to accomplish, resources needed, and reasons for change — all of the above.

questions.text: Heads of educational institutions can appropriately ensure the safety of their students against COVID-19 by the following measures except providing them
options: Hand gloves to protect their hands
Hand sanitizer to sanitize their hands
Water and liquid soap to wash their hands
questions.explanation: Hand gloves are not part of the standard recommended COVID-19 safety measures for schools compared to masks, sanitizer and handwashing.

questions.text: Which one of these questions helps you the least to specify your lesson objectives for student learning, as a teacher?
options: What do I want students to learn?
What do I want them to understand and be able to do at the end of the class?
What is the topic of the lesson?
What will I do to explain the topic?
questions.explanation: Simply naming the lesson topic does the least to specify concrete, measurable learning objectives.

questions.text: Which of these reflective questions would best help the classroom teacher to design learning activities for learning?
options: How will I check whether students know anything about the topic or have any preconceived notions about it?
What are the relevant real-life examples, analogies or situations that can help students understand the topic?
What questions will I ask students to check for understanding?
What will I have students do to demonstrate that they are following?
questions.explanation: Asking what students will do to demonstrate understanding best guides the design of active learning activities.

questions.text: Which of these Ghanaian languages is not approved for teaching and learning in Ghanaian schools?
questions.explanation: Sefwi is not among the Ghanaian languages officially approved for teaching and learning in schools.

questions.text: Which of these learners' attributes is not a major aspect of school bonding? Attachment to
questions.explanation: Attachment to non-teaching staff is not typically identified as a major aspect of learners' school bonding.

questions.text: What reason might make a school unable to maintain adequate educational quality and students' discipline?
questions.explanation: Segregation can undermine a school's ability to maintain adequate educational quality and discipline.

questions.text: Which of the following types of achievement test items can be used to measure high order cognitive skills?
questions.explanation: Essay items are best suited to measuring higher-order cognitive skills such as analysis and synthesis.

questions.text: All of these key terms relate to and/or describe reliability, except:
questions.explanation: Credibility is not one of the standard terms (consistency, dependability, trustworthiness) used to describe reliability.

questions.text: Use the information provided below to answer questions 33 - 35. Bloom's Taxonomy of Educational Objectives lists levels of intellectual understanding, namely: Knowledge, Comprehension, Application, Analysis, Synthesis and Evaluation. These levels of understanding assist in categorizing test questions.  A question which asks learners to 'Restate a concept in their own words' is an example of ……… test question frame.
questions.explanation: Restating a concept in one's own words demonstrates comprehension in Bloom's Taxonomy.

questions.text: A question which asks learners to 'infer from a concept' is an example of ……… test question frame.
questions.explanation: Inferring from a concept requires applying understanding, matching the application level of Bloom's Taxonomy.

questions.text: A question which asks learners 'what is meant by ….?' is an example of ……… test question frame.
questions.explanation: Asking 'what is meant by...' tests recall of a definition, which is a knowledge-level question.

questions.text: Which one of these statements is not correct about examination malpractice?
options: It is a sure way for candidates not to fail in an examination
It may lead to the cancellation of the entire results of a school
People caught in examination leakage may be prosecuted at the law court
The general public may lose confidence in certificates that are awarded to candidates
questions.explanation: Examination malpractice is not a legitimate way to avoid failing — it risks cancelled results, prosecution and loss of public confidence.

questions.text: Programme evaluation is one of the many duties assigned to educational administrators. Which one of the following statements describes summative programme evaluation accurately?
options: It is a process intended to determine if a programme has met its goals
It is a process intended to get input from teachers
It is a process intended to provide information that can be used to improve a programme
questions.explanation: Summative programme evaluation determines whether a programme has met its intended goals.

questions.text: Out of 50 students who took a test, 45 passed. What percentage failed?
questions.explanation: Out of 50 students, 5 failed, which is 10% of the total.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a learning assessment metric for Ghanaian basic schools?
options: Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study (TIMSS)
questions.explanation: The National Examination Assessment (NEA) is Ghana's specific basic-school learning assessment metric.

questions.text: The general name for a scoring guide used to evaluate the quality of students' work is called a/an
questions.explanation: A rubric is the general name for a scoring guide used to evaluate the quality of students' work.

questions.text: The SDG that relates to the education system ensures
options: Equitable and inclusive education for all, especially the girl-child
Improved access and participation in education for all
Inclusive and equitable quality lifelong learning opportunities for all
questions.explanation: SDG 4 specifically calls for inclusive and equitable quality lifelong learning opportunities for all.

questions.text: As ways of mitigating the graduate unemployment issue, the government has introduced the following interventions except
questions.explanation: The National Youth Employment Programme is not one of the specific interventions listed alongside Nation Builders Corps, allowances, and afforestation.

questions.text: All the following are minimum levels of standards every beginner teacher in Ghana must meet according to the components of the National Teachers' Standards (NTS), except
questions.explanation: Ethics is not one of the four core domains of the National Teachers' Standards, which cover knowledge, practice and values.

questions.text: Which of these general competencies envisioned by Ghana's pre-tertiary education curriculum frameworks seems to promote entrepreneurial skills in learners?
questions.explanation: Creativity and Innovation is the competency specifically linked to promoting entrepreneurial skills in Ghana's curriculum framework.

questions.text: A student's ability to analyse issues and situations leading to the resolution of problems is a demonstration of what kind of competence?
questions.explanation: Analysing issues to resolve problems demonstrates Creativity and Innovation competence in the curriculum framework.

questions.text: Which body within the Ghanaian education system has the overall responsibility for education sector policy formulation, planning, evaluation, budgeting and coordinating?
options: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Education holds overall responsibility for policy formulation, planning, evaluation, budgeting and coordination.

questions.text: Which of the following is not part of the major regulatory laws governing the financial administration in schools in Ghana?
options: The Constitution of the Republic of Ghana
questions.explanation: The Constitution is a general governing document, not one of the specific financial administration laws listed alongside the Education Act, Internal Audit Act and PFM Act.

questions.text: Which of these options is not a major aim of the double track intervention which was introduced in senior high schools in Ghana?
options: Create room to accommodate the increase in enrolment
Expand physical school infrastructure and facilities
Increase the number of holidays (especially for teachers)
questions.explanation: Increasing holidays for teachers was not an aim of the double-track system; it was about accommodating enrolment growth.

questions.text: The activity of teachers investigating their own practices and developing useful ideas to improve their practices can be referred to as ……… research.
questions.explanation: Teachers investigating and improving their own classroom practice engage in action research.

questions.text: Which of the following offices of the Ministry of Education houses the Education Management Information Systems (EMIS) data?
questions.explanation: The Statistics, Research and Information Management (SRIM) office houses the EMIS data within the Ministry of Education.

questions.text: Education stakeholders are considered more important to a school when they ......
options: Use of their power in support of the school
Emphasise the urgency of their issues
questions.explanation: Stakeholders gain influence in a school by raising legitimate concerns, not by exerting raw power over it.

questions.text: Which of the following are the main priorities of the Ghana Education Reform Agenda? I. Improve learning outcomes II. Enhanced accountability III. Equality IV. Equity
questions.explanation: The Ghana Education Reform Agenda's main priorities are improving learning outcomes, accountability, and equity.

questions.text: What is the purpose of conducting research?
options: To identify a problem needing solution
To add to or contribute to knowledge
questions.explanation: Research broadly serves to solve problems, identify problems needing solutions, and add to knowledge — all of the above.

questions.text: In which year was the Pre-Tertiary Education Act (1049) enacted?
questions.explanation: The Pre-Tertiary Education Act (Act 1049) was enacted in 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following key qualities are required of a public officer? I. Leadership Skills II. Communication Skills III. Patience and resilience
questions.explanation: Effective public officers typically need leadership skills, communication skills, and patience and resilience together.

questions.text: The degree to which a person identifies with his or her job, actively participates in it, and considers his or her performance as being important to self-worth is referred to as job...
questions.explanation: Job involvement describes the degree to which someone identifies with and invests self-worth in their job performance.

questions.text: Use the scenario below to answer questions 7 and 8. Ama works as a receptionist at an educational institution. Her boss just came through the door and yelled at her, telling her that the front office was a mess and that she needed to get up and clean it immediately. After her boss left the room, Ama grabbed some new papers and violently slammed them into the dustbin.  Which of the following best describes Ama's action?
questions.explanation: Ama's outburst of slamming papers is best described as an emotional reaction (an emotion) to her boss's treatment.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the behaviour of Ama's boss?
questions.explanation: Yelling at a subordinate without explanation reflects impolite, disrespectful behaviour; 'Impolite' best captures the tone here.

questions.text: When decision making is delegated as far down the chain of command as possible in an education system, the system is said to be......
questions.explanation: Delegating decisions down the chain of command describes a decentralised system.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a well-constructed goal of educational organisations? They........
options: are the results of a group decision process
questions.explanation: Well-constructed goals should be precise, realistic and address critical issues — being 'results of a group decision process' is not a defining characteristic.

questions.text: The District Director of Education's Office phone bill in 2020 is GHC 4,200.00. It increases by 10% in 2021 and a further 20% increase in the first six months of 2022. If the Director settles the bill, how much more will she have to pay at the end of June 2022?
questions.explanation: With a 10% then 20% increase calculated in sequence, the bill rises to GHC 5,544.00 by June 2022.

questions.text: Which Act established the Complementary Education Agency (CEA)?
questions.explanation: The Complementary Education Agency (CEA) was established under Act 1055 of 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a key education reform area of the Ministry of Education?
options: Policy on Teachers Education Reforms led by the GTEC through T-TEL
GES institutional and Human Resource Reform
questions.explanation: Global Citizenship Education Reform is not one of the Ministry's four named key reform areas (curriculum, teacher education, and GES institutional reform).

questions.text: What is the following fallacy called? "All ducks love water. Kofi loves water. Therefore, Kofi is a duck."
questions.explanation: Concluding 'Kofi is a duck' from 'ducks love water' and 'Kofi loves water' is the classic fallacy of affirming the consequent.

questions.text: The "best" approach for transformational change in a school is to have the school leader create an atmosphere for change........
options: but let others decide how to initiate a change
but carefully set limits for the program
questions.explanation: Transformational change works best when a leader first establishes and communicates a clear vision.

questions.text: Which one of the following best describes the focus of inclusive education? To increase....
options: Participation of all students in schools including those with disabilities
Participation of all staff in decision making including non-teaching staff
Integration of various subject disciplines such as arts, science and business
Integration of basic, secondary and tertiary systems of education
questions.explanation: Inclusive education focuses on increasing participation of all students, including those with disabilities.

questions.text: The principal strategy adopted for Universal Design for Learning (UDL) is ……..
options: Inviting parents to attend meetings and open days
Giving learners quizzes at the end of every lesson
Asking parents to sign the completed assignments of learners
Adopting multiple ways of representing content to learners
questions.explanation: Universal Design for Learning's principal strategy is offering multiple ways of representing content to learners.

questions.text: Which of the following is not one of the four pillars of secondary education reform in Ghana?
questions.explanation: Improving equality is not one of the four named pillars of Ghana's secondary education reform, which focuses on skills, infrastructure, and fee coverage.

questions.text: Who is the Director-General of the Ghana TVET Service?
questions.explanation: Madam Mawusi Nudekor Awity is the Director-General of the Ghana TVET Service.

questions.text: The plans of school management are often expressed formally in which of the following documents?
questions.explanation: School management plans are typically formalised through budgets.

questions.text: In educational institutions, the idolization of a charismatic leader by followers can lead to……
options: Limiting suggestions for fixes and improvements
Greater understanding of the organisation's mission
questions.explanation: Idolizing a charismatic leader can make followers hesitant to challenge them, limiting suggestions for improvement.

questions.text: In educational settings, since practical considerations make job tryouts for all candidates impracticable, it is necessary to ………. the relative level of job performance for each candidate on the basis of available information.
questions.explanation: Without job tryouts, evaluators must predict candidates' relative job performance from available information.

questions.text: Which one of the following biases refers to the fact that educational decision makers who have strong prior beliefs about an issue tend to make decisions on the basis of these beliefs, even when presented with evidence that their beliefs are wrong?
questions.explanation: Prior hypothesis bias describes decision-makers clinging to existing beliefs despite contrary evidence.

questions.text: An important first step in the process of formulating an education institution's mission is to
options: Identify the client segment served by the institution
Evaluate the institution's most recent performance
Decide what the institution will be like 10 years from now
Answer the question, "What is our business"
questions.explanation: A mission statement formulation process typically begins by answering 'What is our business?'

questions.text: A headmistress wanted her school to keep costs low. Therefore, as an example to others, she drove her own car to school and furnished her office with a plain, steel desk. In this case, the headmistress was displaying her ……
questions.explanation: Leading by example in cost-conscious choices demonstrates the headmistress's commitment to her cause.

questions.text: An argument is sure to be a sound argument if it is a/an
options: Guarantee of truth of its conclusion
questions.explanation: A sound argument must guarantee the truth of its conclusion, combining valid form with true premises.

questions.text: Teachers could be made to be more accountable when they are given the ……..
options: Option to transfer to places where they want to serve
Freedom to select content and methods of teaching
questions.explanation: Teachers become more accountable when they are given opportunities for professional growth.

questions.text: Use the information below to answer questions 28 to 30. The administration of a senior high school wants to know what proportion of their students are satisfied with the library facilities. Eighteen (18) library staff are keen to help. They select 200 students in the library during the first week of the exam period and ask them to fill in a questionnaire on satisfaction with the library.  What is the population that the sample was selected from?
options: The 200 students who completed the questionnaire
All the students and library staff
All students in the library during the first week of the exam period
questions.explanation: The population sampled from is all students present in the library during that first exam week, since that is where the 200 were drawn from.

questions.text: The survey conducted by the library staff at the senior high school — what is the population that the school administration is interested in?
options: The 200 students who completed the questionnaire
All the students and the library staff
All students in the library during the first week of the exam period
All the students enrolled at the senior high school
questions.explanation: The population the school administration is actually interested in is all students enrolled at the school, beyond just those in the library that week.

questions.text: What is the sample size for the survey?
questions.explanation: The 200 students who completed the questionnaire constitute the sample size for this survey.

questions.text: Who won the best teacher (Leadership and Administration) in the 2022 Ghana Teacher Prize?
questions.explanation: Ivy Asantewa Owusu won the Leadership and Administration category of the 2022 Ghana Teacher Prize.

questions.text: In a teacher-centered school, the headteacher undertakes all the following activities to enhance teaching and learning except……
options: Motivating and sustaining teachers' interest in teaching
Encouraging teachers to develop lesson plans that build on existing knowledge
Encouraging teachers to avoid tests because they demoralize students
Empowering teachers to involve each learner in the teaching/learning process
questions.explanation: A teacher-centred headteacher would not encourage avoiding tests, since assessment supports learning rather than simply demoralising students.

questions.text: The general competence intended by Ghana's pre-tertiary education curriculum framework to promote entrepreneurial skills in learners is
questions.explanation: Creativity and Innovation is the competence in Ghana's curriculum framework tied to entrepreneurial skill development.

questions.text: The type of test that measures the performance of learners against the standards covered in the curriculum is called…….a/an
questions.explanation: A criterion-referenced test measures learner performance against the standards set out in the curriculum.

questions.text: Which of the following is not one of the core domains of the national teachers standards?
questions.explanation: Ethics is not one of the four core domains of the national teachers standards, which cover values, practice and knowledge.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a tool for the formative assessment in the school system?
questions.explanation: An inventory is not a standard formative assessment tool compared with projects, oral questions, and MCQs.

questions.text: Which of the following relates to the affective domain of students' behaviour?
questions.explanation: Stereotypes, feelings and attitudes all fall under the affective domain of student behaviour.

questions.text: The topmost responsibility of a headteacher is to:
questions.explanation: The topmost responsibility of a headteacher is to provide leadership for learning.

questions.text: The first important step in teaching is…
options: Knowing the background of the students
questions.explanation: Effective teaching begins with knowing the background of the students before planning lessons.

questions.text: In what year did GES replace promotion interviews with promotion examinations?
questions.explanation: GES replaced promotion interviews with promotion examinations starting in 2020.

questions.text: The main objective of classroom assessment is to ………..
options: Report on learners' performance to parents
questions.explanation: The main objective of classroom assessment is to improve teaching and learning, not just to report or compare.

questions.text: A teacher teaches in a remote school where newspapers are delivered irregularly. With the importance of keeping the students abreast with current affairs in mind, what is the best way to keep the students updated?
options: Urge the pupils to listen to stories circulating in the community
Try all available means to get all the newspapers delivered to the school
Gather back issues of newspapers and let pupils compile them
Encourage the pupils to listen to the daily broadcasts from a radio
questions.explanation: In areas without reliable newspapers, radio broadcasts offer the most practical way to keep students updated on current affairs.

questions.text: Learners are most likely to be intrinsically motivated to learn and master subject matter when they……
options: Perceive that their performance will compare favorably with that of their peers
Know they will receive positive reinforcement for achieving instructional objectives
Know they will be tested for their understanding of the content in the near future
Believe that the work they are doing is interesting and relates to their own lives
questions.explanation: Learners are most intrinsically motivated when the work feels interesting and relevant to their own lives.

questions.text: The fundamental aim of supervision is to help……
questions.explanation: Supervision's fundamental aim is to help children learn more effectively, which is the ultimate purpose behind supporting teachers.

questions.text: To make learning effective, an instructional goal must be meaningful in terms of……….
questions.explanation: Instructional goals must be meaningful in terms of students' own needs and purposes to be effective.

questions.text: Procedures used to determine a learner's abilities are referred to as ……….
questions.explanation: A maximum performance test is used to determine a learner's abilities at their best effort.

questions.text: What are the three components of an educational process?
questions.explanation: The educational process rests on teaching, learning and practice as its three components.

questions.text: Which one of the following does not characterize a well-planned lesson?
options: Varied teaching and learning resources are utilized to promote learning
Varied procedures and activities are undertaken by the pupils
Lesson objectives are specific, measurable and achievable
Lesson notes are vetted by school heads
questions.explanation: Vetting lesson notes by school heads is an administrative check, not itself a defining feature of a well-planned lesson.

questions.text: The capitation grant provided to a school can be used for the ….
options: Attend to sanitation and minor repairs and maintenance
questions.explanation: The capitation grant is intended, among other uses, to help schools organise extra classes for pupils.

questions.text: What is the most important factor a teacher should consider in selecting and utilizing instructional materials?
options: Degree of interest on the part of the students
questions.explanation: Selecting instructional materials should be guided primarily by the objectives of the lesson.

questions.text: Which of the following best illustrates a teacher applying a constructivist approach to student learning?
options: A language arts teacher provides students with a concrete reward each time they turn in a written assignment that is free of errors
A math teacher has students use hands-on materials and real-world problems to acquire new concepts and practice skills
A science teacher demonstrates the correct procedures for performing complex experiments before having students perform the experiments
A social studies teacher uses visual aids and logical progression of ideas when presenting lessons about new or unfamiliar topics
questions.explanation: Constructivism has learners build understanding themselves through hands-on materials and real-world problem solving.

questions.text: A JHS teacher gives students a term project involving research, interviewing people, writing a report and making a group presentation. Which strategy should the teacher use to help students successfully carry out their projects?
options: Explaining to students how the objectives of the project fit into a larger instructional plan
Organizing project tasks in a step-by-step sequence and providing students with directions and reminders for completing each step
Putting students into groups and scheduling regular times for them to meet
Reassuring students that they possess all of the skills and abilities needed to complete the project tasks
questions.explanation: Helping students see how project objectives connect to the broader instructional plan gives purpose and direction to their work.

questions.text: In a typical teaching and learning environment, students are most likely to be intrinsically motivated to learn when they …
options: Anticipate that they will receive positive rewards for achieving instructional objectives
Are interested in what they are learning and understand how it relates to their own lives
Know that they will be writing a test or examination in the near future
Perceive that their performance compares favorably with that of peers engaged in the same tasks
questions.explanation: Intrinsic motivation arises when learners find the material personally interesting and relevant to their own lives.

questions.text: The Free SHS programme in Ghana is funded by the …….
questions.explanation: The Free SHS programme is financed through the Annual Budget Funding Amount (ABFA).

questions.text: Alhaji Musa has recently been appointed head of an educational institution. He thought of crafting a statement giving a dramatic look at what the entire school will be like at a distant point in the future, say five to ten years. This statement is called a/an …
questions.explanation: A statement describing a future, aspirational picture of the school years ahead is a vision statement.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about effective classroom management is false? Classroom management involves …….
options: Planning ahead of the first day of class
Teachers having at least four rules to guide them
The difference between calm productivity and total class disorder
The same strategies but may vary in the techniques used for each class
questions.explanation: Per the answer key, this option is identified as the false statement among the listed characteristics of effective classroom management.

questions.text: Global citizenship education is a form of … that involves students' active participation in projects that address global issues of social, political and economic development.
questions.explanation: Global citizenship education is best understood as a form of civic education focused on active participation in global issues.

questions.text: Which of the following affirms that quality is at the heart of education and sets out the desirable characteristics for the various components of quality education — learners, content and systems?
options: Salamanca Statement and Frame for Action
questions.explanation: The Salamanca Statement and Framework for Action set out desirable characteristics for quality education components.

questions.text: Which of the following in Ghana has the objective of equitable educational opportunity and the prioritization of the disadvantaged in society?
questions.explanation: Ghana's inclusive education system specifically targets equitable opportunity and prioritising disadvantaged learners.

questions.text: When making important administrative decisions, it helps to ……
options: Enlist advice from the assistant school head
Give teachers a chance to make their contributions
Implement changes as quickly as possible
Reward teachers who adapt more quickly
questions.explanation: Involving teachers in contributing to decisions improves the quality and acceptance of administrative decisions.

questions.text: The standards specified in the new GES Curriculum for Basic schools (implemented September 2019 in Ghana) are based on what Ghana requires of its workforce and on demands of globalization, so graduates can compare in the international job market. Which goal of curriculum development does this reflect?
options: Development of a sense of civic responsibility
Preservation of national resource and cultural values
questions.explanation: Preparing graduates who can compete internationally reflects the goal of a globally competitive Ghanaian workforce.

questions.text: Ensuring high teacher morale is important because teachers with high morale …..
options: Are more likely to remain on the job in spite of challenges
Ask more interesting questions of their students
questions.explanation: High morale is chiefly linked to teacher retention, helping them persist through challenges.

questions.text: During teacher evaluation, circuit supervisors or school heads need to take objective, evidence-based notes to share with teachers in post-observation and guide discussions. Which statement best illustrates such notes?
options: In a class of 42, the teacher calls on one student to answer four out of ten questions asked
The teacher is highly responsive to the cultural and other types of student diversity in the class
The teacher makes little or no effort to make instruction relevant to student interest and needs
Throughout the lesson, the teacher uses a variety of strategies to monitor students' understanding
questions.explanation: An objective, evidence-based note records specific observed actions like varied strategies used to monitor understanding, rather than vague judgements.

questions.text: A school head is about to take over leadership of a low-performing school. One of the school head's first goals will be to evaluate teacher quality in the school. The school head can best begin this process by
options: Arranging to observe instruction in each class
Comparing students' grades in each subject area across classrooms
Having each teacher complete a teacher self-evaluation
Interviewing each teacher about his or her teaching practices
questions.explanation: Comparing grade patterns across classrooms offers a quick, data-based first step before deeper individual evaluation.

questions.text: The basic assumption that supervision has an 'expert tag' attached to it means the supervisor…
options: Should ensure students have the requisite qualifications before they are admitted
Should ensure that teachers have the minimum academic qualification
Should ensure that teachers have lots of workload
questions.explanation: The 'expert tag' of supervision implies verifying that teachers meet the minimum required academic qualifications.

questions.text: A school head has been transferred to a failing school. To turn it around, the school head can best avoid early mistakes and promote a smooth transition by taking which action first?
options: Communicating a willingness to refer initially to the experience and judgement of long-time staff
Holding discussions with many stakeholders to learn about local values, views and priorities
Presenting for discussion a comprehensive, research-supported plan for improved student achievement
Seeking information from the previous school head about leadership strategies that did and did not work
questions.explanation: Consulting broadly with stakeholders first helps a new leader understand local context before proposing changes.

questions.text: Which one of the following factors should an educator consider as most important when evaluating a programme?
options: The cost involved in carrying out the evaluation of the programme
The uses of the evaluation results
Where and when the evaluation will take place
Who the stakeholders of the programme are
questions.explanation: Identifying the programme's stakeholders is foundational, since it shapes what the evaluation should investigate and for whom.

questions.text: Which action would you take to attain a high level of consistency in scoring students' responses to assessment tasks? By …
options: Constantly following the scoring guide as the scripts are graded
Grading responses for all items for each script before the next script
Regularly referring to previously scored items when scoring new items
Scoring the response based on knowledge of the student's identity
questions.explanation: Consistently applying the scoring guide throughout grading is the most reliable way to maintain scoring consistency.

questions.text: A student-teacher who had a grade B+ in assessment in school could not write good items for an end-of-term examination. The head teacher questioned the teacher as to whether he really took part in the assessment course. Which characteristic of a good test might have informed the head teacher's question?
questions.explanation: The concern is whether the test items actually measure what they are intended to measure — that is, validity.

questions.text: Which of the following purposes of assessment is often associated with a letter, grade or number?
questions.explanation: Assessment of learning is summative and is usually expressed as a letter grade or number.

questions.text: A criterion-referenced assessment would most likely be used to …….
options: Decide a student's position in an integrated science end-of-term examination
Determine if the student qualifies for special-education service
Determine whether an individual student is meeting curriculum standards
Select a student for a government scholarship
questions.explanation: Criterion-referenced assessment measures whether a student meets fixed curriculum standards, not their rank among peers.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are false? I. It is easy to achieve the broad national goals of education when curriculum development is decentralized. II. Students who follow a decentralized curriculum in deprived school districts are likely to be disadvantaged in the market.
questions.explanation: Statement I is true — decentralisation actually complicates achieving broad national goals — so statement II is identified as the false one here per the key.

questions.text: The following constitute special units under the GES except ……
questions.explanation: Science Resource Centre is not one of the recognised special units under GES, unlike the others listed.

questions.text: The tenure of office of members of the GES council is …..
questions.explanation: Members of the GES Council serve a tenure of three years.

questions.text: Transfer grants payable is equivalent to …….
questions.explanation: Transfer grants are calculated as equivalent to two months' gross salary.

questions.text: The government of Ghana mainstreamed KG into basic education in line with the recommendations of the ….
questions.explanation: Mainstreaming KG into basic education followed the recommendations of the Dakar World Forum for Education.

questions.text: The role of the School Management Committees (SMCs) and heads in managing the capitation grant includes all the following except to ensure …..
options: Effective utilization of the capitation grant
Implementation of activities provided in the SPIP
School opens a special bank account
questions.explanation: Implementing SPIP activities is not specifically an SMC/head role in managing the capitation grant, unlike the financial accountability duties listed.

questions.text: In the computerized schools' selection and placement system, all the following are used except the score of ….
options: All subjects taken by BECE candidates
Two best subjects of BECE candidates
questions.explanation: The CSSPS uses core subjects plus best elective subjects, not the scores of all subjects taken.

questions.text: The main purpose of the policy on girl-child education by government is to ensure that
options: All girls of school-going age go to and stay in school
All girls of school-going age register in school
Girls in rural areas have equal access to school
questions.explanation: The girl-child education policy's main purpose is ensuring girls not only enroll but also stay in school.

questions.text: The scheme of service of teachers refers to the …….
options: Activities of the teachers for the term approved by the school head
Outline of lesson plans presented to circuit supervisors
Scheme of work prepared by the teacher for the term
Various ranks a teacher passes through in the teaching profession
questions.explanation: The 'scheme of service' describes the career progression ranks a teacher passes through, not lesson planning documents.

questions.text: One of the students in a class hardly talks in class. How would you encourage him to express himself?
options: By encouraging children to take part in activities
By giving good marks to those who express themselves well
By organizing discussions around classroom activities
By organizing an educational games programme which will make children feel like speaking
questions.explanation: A games-based approach can lower a shy student's inhibitions and make speaking feel natural and low-pressure.

questions.text: A teacher should use appropriate methods, techniques and sound principles of learning such as … I. Building on past learning or previous knowledge and positive reinforcement II. Providing guidance and practice in class before independent practice III. Motivating and sustaining pupils' interest IV. Involving each learner in the teaching/learning process V. Distributing evaluative questions evenly
options: I, II, III and V only
I, II, III, IV and V
questions.explanation: Effective teaching draws on all five listed principles together, not just a subset.

questions.text: A curriculum is the sum-total of a school's efforts to influence a child's….
questions.explanation: Curriculum is broadly defined as the sum of a school's efforts to shape a child's behaviour.

questions.text: Which of the following is a teacher-centered model that focuses on students' activities being guided by the teacher?
questions.explanation: The directive model is teacher-centred, with the teacher closely guiding student activities.

questions.text: Any method of teaching which involves two or more students can be termed as
questions.explanation: Teaching methods involving two or more students collaborating are termed group work.

questions.text: According to Skinnerian Operant Conditioning Theory, a negative reinforcement is …………
options: Avoiding an undesirable stimulus to increase the likelihood of a behaviour
Adding a pleasant stimulus to increase the likelihood of a behaviour
Removing a pleasant stimulus to decrease the likelihood of a behaviour
Adding an unpleasant stimulus to decrease the likelihood of a behaviour
questions.explanation: Negative reinforcement involves removing or avoiding an undesirable stimulus to increase a behaviour's likelihood.

questions.text: In classroom management, the teacher's strategies and techniques must be ………
questions.explanation: Effective classroom management requires varied strategies and techniques suited to different situations.

questions.text: The ultimate purpose of supervision is to ensure ……….
questions.explanation: Supervision ultimately exists to advance the welfare of the child, beyond just monitoring teachers.

questions.text: Which Sustainable Development Goal is directly related to education?
questions.explanation: SDG 4 is the goal directly focused on quality education.

questions.text: What does the Sustainable Development Goal directly related to education state?
options: Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education for all and promote lifelong learning opportunities
Eliminate all school fees globally by 2025
Provide free tertiary education for all nations
Achieve universal literacy through digital platforms only
questions.explanation: SDG 4 specifically calls for inclusive, equitable quality education and lifelong learning opportunities for all.

questions.text: The Computerized School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS) improves the manual system of selecting and placing qualified BECE candidates into public and private senior high, technical and vocational institutes, and is administered by………..
options: The National Council for Curriculum and Assessment
questions.explanation: The CSSPS, which replaced the manual placement process, is administered by the Ghana Education Service.

questions.text: The United Nations General Assembly proclaimed 24th January as the International Day of Education, in celebration of the role of ………..
questions.explanation: The International Day of Education celebrates education's role in fostering peace and development.

questions.text: The rationale of education planning in our education system is ………..
questions.explanation: Education planning in Ghana is grounded in the principles of access, equity, and quality.

questions.text: The primary role of a mentoring teacher in the school of a pre-service teacher is most appropriately described as ……….
questions.explanation: The mentoring teacher's core role, as the name suggests, is to mentor the pre-service teacher.

questions.text: The basic purpose of instructional supervision is for ………….
questions.explanation: Instructional supervision fundamentally aims to promote effective teaching and learning.

questions.text: When the school head directs an investigation into suspected fraud, the only authorities to impose sanctions are………..
options: The School Management Committee and Board of Governors
The Police Service and Ministry of Education
questions.explanation: Sanctions following a fraud investigation are imposed by the School Management Committee and Board of Governors.

questions.text: The method of obtaining information to judge the worth of a curriculum while it is being implemented is known as …………
questions.explanation: Judging a curriculum's worth during implementation is the function of curriculum evaluation.

questions.text: The ability for students to use an appropriate rule or principle to help solve a problem without being prompted is specified in the cognitive domain of Bloom's Taxonomy as …………
questions.explanation: Independently applying a rule or principle to solve a problem corresponds to the Application level of Bloom's Taxonomy.

questions.text: The type of assessment used to determine students' strengths and weaknesses for correction and remediation is known as ……
questions.explanation: Diagnostic assessment specifically identifies strengths and weaknesses to guide remediation.

questions.text: In the chain of command of the GES headquarters, the Director-General is the Chief Executive accountable to the ………
options: National Council for Curriculum and Assessment
questions.explanation: The Director-General, as Chief Executive, is accountable to the Ghana Education Service Council.

questions.text: What is the core function of the National Inspectorate Board?
options: To undertake school inspection, evaluate schools, and set and enforce standards
To recruit and post teachers nationwide
questions.explanation: The National Inspectorate Board's core function is inspecting and evaluating schools and enforcing standards.

questions.text: The main role of the Education Sector Analysis (ESA) is to ……….
options: Identify the progress made in the pre-tertiary institutions
questions.explanation: The Education Sector Analysis is mainly concerned with identifying progress made across pre-tertiary institutions.

questions.text: The GES was established in the year 1974 as a national organization under the Ministry of Education (MOE) by the ………. of 1995.
questions.explanation: GES was formally established under Act 506 of 1995.

questions.text: It is important for teachers to know the code of conduct because …….
options: It provides guidance for teachers in the performance of their duties
It replaces the need for supervision
It exempts teachers from disciplinary procedures
questions.explanation: The code of conduct exists to guide teachers in properly performing their duties.

questions.text: ………….project launched in 1997 on a pilot basis in 12 Districts (out of a total of 110) and three Regional Offices was to improve the collection, processing and analysis of educational data in order to make reliable information available for decision making at all levels of the education system.
options: Ghana Integrated Financial Management Information System (GIFMIS)
questions.explanation: EMIS was piloted from 1997 to improve collection, processing and analysis of educational data for decision-making.

questions.text: Which system supports management of public sector budgetary, financial, and accounting operations and promotes better public financial management (PFM) with a centralized registry of public sector revenues and expenditures?
options: Ghana Integrated Financial Management Information System (GIFMIS)
Ghana Financial Management Systems for Education (GFMSE)
questions.explanation: GIFMIS centralises public sector budgeting, financial and accounting operations across government, including revenues and expenditures.

questions.text: At the Education Directorate, maternity and paternity leaves are prepared by
questions.explanation: Maternity and paternity leave documentation at the Education Directorate is prepared by the Welfare Officer.

questions.text: The following explain why Teacher Management is important except
options: Teachers are the main resource of any education system and require specific management
Teachers have a strong influence on the quality of education
Poor management of Teachers can lead to Teachers moving to the rural areas
Teacher management also plays a key role in achieving the qualitative goals of the Education 2030 agenda, as underlined by the Incheon declaration
questions.explanation: Poor teacher management typically drives teachers away from, not toward, rural or deprived postings, making this the incorrect rationale among the options.

questions.text: ………………………………………………are paid to an employee who is required by the Supervising Officer to undertake duties of a special nature requiring additional responsibilities.
questions.explanation: Extra duty allowances specifically compensate employees assigned special additional responsibilities by a supervising officer.

questions.text: ……………………………………. refers to allocation of allowance for any hours worked by an employee that exceed their normally scheduled working hours.
questions.explanation: Compensation for hours worked beyond the normal schedule is specifically termed overtime allowance.

questions.text: Government of Ghana is introducing a ………………………………………….. of GH¢1,200 per year for professional teachers and GH¢600 per year for non-professional teachers to deepen their commitment and spur professional growth.
questions.explanation: This differentiated annual allowance for professional versus non-professional teachers is identified here as the Teacher Retention Allowance (TRA).

questions.text: At what stage does Ghana Education Service work in collaboration with the Ghana Health Service?
options: Issuance or Renewal of NHIS cards
Immunization/Vaccination of pupils against sicknesses and diseases
Provision of First Aid Boxes to schools
questions.explanation: GES and GHS collaborate on school health programmes, notably the immunization and vaccination of pupils.

questions.text: GIFMIS is an IT based system for budget management and accounting that is being implemented by the Government of Ghana to improve Public Expenditure Management processes, enhance greater accountability and transparency across Ministries and Departments. What is GIFMIS?
options: Government Integral Financial Management Information System
Ghana Integrated Financial Management Information System
Government Integrated Fiscal Management Information System
Government Integrated Financial Management Information Software
